vocabulary.example: We are excited about the trip.
I feel nervous before a test.

grammar.point: I feel / I am + emotion adjective
grammar.point_ko: 감정 표현: I feel / I am + 형용사
grammar.explanation_en: To express emotions, use 'I am + adjective' or 'I feel + adjective': 'I am happy' and 'I feel happy' both work and mean the same thing. Ask others with 'How do you feel?' or 'Are you okay?'.
grammar.explanation_ko: 감정을 표현할 때는 'I am + 형용사' 또는 'I feel + 형용사'를 씁니다: 'I am happy'와 'I feel happy'는 둘 다 쓸 수 있고 같은 뜻입니다. 상대방에게 물을 때는 'How do you feel?' 또는 'Are you okay?'를 씁니다.

examples.en: She is nervous about the exam.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: You look tired. Are you okay?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: Yes, I'm just a little tired. I feel excited about the weekend though!
dialogue.line_ko: 네, 그냥 좀 피곤해요. 그래도 주말이 기대돼서 신나요!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: What are you doing this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: I'm going hiking. I'm a little nervous too, it's my first time.
dialogue.line_ko: 등산 갈 거예요. 처음이라 좀 긴장도 돼요.

reading.title: A Big Day
reading.text: Today is my first day at a new job. I feel nervous, but also excited. This morning, I was a little tired because I didn't sleep well. My friend told me, 'Don't worry, you will do great!' Now I feel happy and ready.
reading.text_ko: 오늘은 새 직장에서의 첫날이에요. 긴장되지만 동시에 신나요. 오늘 아침에는 잠을 잘 못 자서 조금 피곤했어요. 친구가 '걱정하지 마, 넌 잘할 거야!'라고 말해줬어요. 이제는 기분이 좋고 준비된 느낌이에요.

explanation.en: The text says 'Today is my first day at a new job.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'my first day at a new job'이라고 나옵니다.

explanation.en: The text says 'because I didn't sleep well.'
The text says 'Now I feel happy and ready.'
explanation.ko: 본문에 'Now I feel happy and ready.'라고 나옵니다.
